## Critique
- claim-1: Correctly identifies the exact original target: minimality of both stated families, not a transition identity or broader presentation theorem.
- claim-2: Adequately grounded by [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 187-195] and [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235].
- claim-3: The parameter audit is complete. The hypotheses imply
  \[
  q-i=n-r-s+t-1\ge0,\qquad r-j=t-1\ge0,
  \]
  hence \(1\le i\le q\), \(1\le j\le r\). Also \(r<n\) and \(s<n\), since equality in either would contradict \(t\le r,s\) and \(t>r+s-n\). For
  \[
  (r^\vee,s^\vee,t^\vee)=(q,n-s,n-r-s+t),
  \]
  one has
  \[
  1\le t^\vee\le r^\vee,\quad t^\vee\le s^\vee\le n,\quad
  t^\vee-(r^\vee+s^\vee-n)=t>0.
  \]
  Direct substitution gives
  \[
  i^\vee=j,\qquad j^\vee=i,\qquad
  a^\vee=\min(r-j,q-i)=a,\qquad b^\vee=b.
  \]
- claim-4: Correct. Conjugation bijects partitions inside \(q^r\) with those inside \(r^q\), and therefore bijects the complementary Schur bases. Since \(\omega\) permutes the integral Schur basis and preserves weight, the induced quotient isomorphism is integral and graded.
- claim-5: Correct. The relevant shape identities are
  \[
  (i^j)'=j^i,\qquad
  ((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})'=(j^i,b^a),
  \]
  and, conversely,
  \[
  (i^j,b^a)'=((j+a)^b,j^{i-b}).
  \]
  Inclusion is preserved by conjugation, so the interval description gives \(\omega(J_v)=J_{v^\vee}\) and a bijection \(\omega(G_R(v))=G_L(v^\vee)\). When \(a=0\), the two intervals are the singletons \(i^j\) and \(j^i\), so no boundary exception remains.
- claim-6: Correct. The graded quotient isomorphism maps the source and target positive-degree ideals to one another and hence maps \(A_+J_v\) onto \(A_+J_{v^\vee}\). The lower-family integral basis from `research-attempt-research-plan-task-296-1` therefore pulls back to an integral basis represented by \(G_R(v)\). Generation transfers simultaneously from the conjugate lower family. A proper subfamily cannot span the corresponding quotient basis and consequently cannot generate the ideal. The same reasoning applies directly to \(G_L(v)\), including \(a=0\).
- claim-7: [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 207-211] explicitly transfers generation and minimal generation between the Grassmannian contraction and the original flag-variety basic ideal.

The requested target is established: the dependency-closed conjugation argument proves the full original two-family minimality conjecture. No universal transition identity or finite computation is used.
